title: Frontend components, state, API client
idea: Frontend LLD decides the screens, which component owns each piece of state, and one API client that handles errors, retries and the Idempotency-Key.
points: The page component loads data; display children like SlotCard only render props.
Server data, form input and request status are separate state, each owned once.
One reducer, a pure function of state and event, owns a screen's steps.
The client retries only transient failures and keeps one key per intent.

edges.label: owns
edges.caption: DoctorPage calls `useSlots`, which holds the server data and its loading and error flags.

edges.label: owns
edges.caption: DoctorPage owns the screen reducer: a pure function from state and event to the next state.
SlotList gets slots as props. Its loading, empty and error views are designed before the happy path.
Each SlotCard shows one slot and keeps no state of its own.
BookSlotButton owns only its request phase and its Idempotency-Key.

edges.label: GET
edges.caption: Loading slots goes through the client, which retries 5xx and network errors.

edges.label: POST
edges.caption: Booking uses the same client; every retry sends the same key.
The client is the only code that knows URLs, headers and the error shape.

edges.label: dispatch
edges.caption: On success the button calls `onBooked`, which dispatches `booked`; DoctorPage then routes to the confirmation page.

code.title: API client with retries
code.caption: Pure client logic against a fake server, so it runs in the page. The wait is printed, not slept.

walk.text: One key per call, reused by every retry; the caller can pass its own.
A thrown fetch becomes status 0, a network error, like any other result.
Any 2xx is success; the UI gets data, never a raw response.
Only network errors and 5xx retry; a 4xx returns at once.
Exponential backoff doubles the wait; production adds random jitter.
The fake server stores the booking, then loses the first reply.
Load slots, book SL-1 through a lost reply, then hit a taken slot.

code.title: BookSlotButton component
code.caption: A React component that owns one request's state. Not run here.

walk.text: One Idempotency-Key per booking intent, kept across re-renders and manual retries.
Ignore clicks while submitting, then mark the request in flight.
Success hands the appointment to the parent; this component stores nothing more.
A taken slot and a failure get different messages and next steps.
The disabled button is the visible guard; the key is the real one.

pitfalls: Do not copy server data into many components; keep one owner and pass props.
Never retry a POST without an Idempotency-Key; a lost reply becomes a double booking.
Never auto-retry a 409; show the user what to do next.

quiz.q: In the run, what does book SL-1 finally return?
options: ok with AP-1, after one retry
ok with AP-2, after one retry
An error: SLOT_TAKEN on the retry
quiz.why: The server stored AP-1 under key-1 before the reply was lost. The retry sends key-1 again, so the server replays AP-1 with 200.

takeaway: One owner per piece of state; one client for every request.
